page: OVHcloud d2-2 is an entry-tier virtual server within the Discovery line, featuring 1 shared x86_64 vCPU based on the Intel Haswell architecture clocked at 2.0 GHz. The virtual machine operates on a KVM hypervisor and is allocated 2.0 GB of system memory. Bundled local storage is provisioned as a 25 GB NVMe SSD. The configuration includes zero dedicated GPUs, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and a 0 Gbps network bandwidth baseline.

Benchmark evaluations position this instance in the lowest decile across compute and memory operations. The shared single core generated a PassMark CPU score of 1039.79 and a stress-ng score of 850.47. In data processing workloads, memory bandwidth reached 8.34 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 7.57 GB/sec for uncached writes, while cached reads peaked at 69.49 GB/sec. Application testing recorded 0.96 million Redis SET operations per second and 0.97 GB/sec throughput for static web serving.

The primary architectural constraint is the shared CPU allocation paired with an older instruction pipeline lacking modern AVX-512 and AMX extensions. However, the integration of local NVMe SSD storage provides responsive disk operations relative to the low overall resource envelope. The server is suited for software development testing, sandbox environments, educational setups, low-traffic static web servers, and non-critical background jobs with minimal resource requirements.
description: OVHcloud d2-2 is an entry-level virtual server belonging to the Discovery family, designed for low-intensity cloud computing. It features 1 shared x86_64 vCPU based on the Intel Haswell architecture running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 2.0 GB of system memory. Storage is provisioned via 25 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD capacity, while GPU acceleration is absent. In performance evaluations, the shared core and legacy architecture place it in the lower tiers of standard compute benchmarks, reflecting a PassMark CPU result of 1039.79 and a Redis SET throughput of 0.96 million operations per second. Given its resource limits, shared CPU model, and lack of bundled public IPv4 networking, the d2-2 offers a compact resource footprint suitable for development sandboxes, internal tooling, educational labs, lightweight microservices, and modest background workloads that do not demand sustained compute performance.
